confidence_notes: I found only a few web sources on Hampi prices. They include aggregated budget tables from TripBase and Oysterlist (inexpensive meal about $1.5-2, coffee about $1, beer about $2, cocktail about $4) and undated or older traveller blogs (beer about INR 180 per bottle at guesthouses, curry with rice about INR 200, thalis and South Indian meals about INR 50-250). Several of these sources are clearly years old. Because Karnataka raised excise duties, the food and drink anchors have been adjusted upward to an estimated mid-2026 level, using roughly INR 88-90 per USD. Draft beer is effectively not available in Hampi. Alcohol is restricted near the temple and bazaar side and is usually served only on request at guesthouses across the river, or at hotel bars in Kamalapura and Hospet. The beer anchor therefore reflects a standard bottled Kingfisher-type serving of about INR 250. I found no cocktail or wine-by-the-glass prices for any Hampi or Hospet venue. Those two anchors come from the local beer price plus typical Indian hotel-bar pricing in small towns, so they are the least reliable. The cappuccino price is an estimate for backpacker cafes and is not confirmed by a source. The accommodation anchors are model estimates from general knowledge and were not checked against any listings. July is the hot, wet off-season, so room rates are probably below the October-February peak.
comparable_city_reasoning: Treated as a low-cost rural heritage and backpacker destination in Karnataka. Food and accommodation prices resemble other small backpacker hubs in South India, such as Gokarna. Alcohol and three-star hotel prices are based on nearby Hospet (Hosapete) and Kamalapura, where most bars and the formal hotel stock are.
